newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain estimates Q4 GDP up 2.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain estimates Q4 GDP up 2.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The Bank of Spain estimated gross domestic product grew 2.5 percent year on year in the fourth quarter of 1996, versus a rise of 2.2 percent in the third quarter.
The estimates are included in the central bank's January economic report, released on Tuesday.
The central bank also estimated full year 1996 GDP grew around 2.2 percent, while private consumption rose around two percent in the same period.
"Fourth quarter GDP could see real growth of around 2.5 percent year on year, with the industrial sectors -- excluding construction -- having seen the biggest recovery," the report said.

Although the 1996 rise in GDP was lower than the 3.0 percent growth rate in the previous year, the slowdown experienced in quarterly growth rates experienced over the course of 1995 was over, the bank said.
As regards inflation, the Bank of Spain warned that the slowdown in services prices may have bottomed out while energy prices may be picking up.

"(These two elements) are the most worrying factors regarding the continuation of the slowdown in inflation this year," it said, quoting a 40 percent rise in the price of crude in November year-on-year as an example of this.
The bank highlighted a recovery in private consumption, estimated to have grown two percent in 1996, and a strong slowdown in fixed capital investment.
It added that the most significant figure in 1996 was the positive contribution (0.5 percentage points) of foreign demand to GDP growth, rather than a negative contribution as in the prior year.
